summary: R1 IS GENUINELY CLOSED AS BEHAVIOUR, measured not trusted: I repeated the 2000-seed toggle over a fixed 120-call sequence (unreachable 0 -> 0.05, ambiguousPut/duplicatePut held at 0.05). On seed 1 ambiguousPut now fires at [k36,k49,k77,k93] with unreachable off and at [k36,k49,k77,k93] with it on -- identical, against round 3's [36,49,77,93] vs [39,54,82,100]. Across 2000 seeds 1010 recorded lists still differ, and I checked what the difference IS: the on-set is a strict SUBSET of the off-set in 2000/2000 seeds, and every removed entry is a key where unreachable fired on that same call (0 unexplained removals). So the draws are aligned and the only change is precedence masking, which is the behaviour criterion 1 wants. The stat/get/list asymmetry (they draw only the unreachable stream) is SOUND, not a remaining aliasing hole: for a fixed call sequence the ambiguous/duplicate stream positions depend only on the number of putIfAbsent/putIfMatch calls and not on any probability, so toggling a class cannot move them. R2 IS CLOSED FOR THREE OF ITS FOUR ITEMS, measured in situ: scramble -> seed*3+stream fails theTHREEFaultStreamsAreINDEPENDENT... (1 of 9); scramble -> 0L fails that test plus the same-seed-replay test (2 of 9); deleting the duplicate delegate.putIfAbsent fails aDUPLICATEDPutREALLYREACHES... (the CountingBinStore delta of 2 genuinely observes the delegate, since puts() is incremented before delegating); and all three guard mutants die -- NaN-accepting (p<0||p>1) kills the guard test, p<1.0 kills 6 tests, p>0.0 kills 7 -- so both range ends and NaN are pinned. Offline I also confirmed the decorrelation test's [expected/3, expected*3] band rejects seed+stream, seed*31+stream, Objects.hash and seed-only on all four draws, for all three stream pairs. R5 is closed (SimulatedClock is not staged). R6, R7 and R8 are unchanged and still open as minors already recorded at 2f893cc26126 -- Injected.kind is still a free-form String, the file still contains no word about thread confinement while `injected` is a plain ArrayList whose List.copyOf can tear under a concurrent add (the headline SEEDED AND REPLAYABLE claim depends on single-threaded use and still does not say so), and putIfAbsent still materialises the body on the no-fault path while putIfMatch does not. Per rule 11 I am not re-filing them. WHAT IS STILL WRONG: the fourth R2 item was not closed -- the R1 fix itself is pinned by nothing, and the new test was deliberately scoped to exclude the control flow the defect lived in (V1). And the backlog, which is what R3 and R4 were about, has three new factual problems: the M4.12 row undercounts its own tests by three, and the three it omits are exactly the R2 pins (V2); the newly created M4.16 row claims an ADR that exists nowhere in the tree (V3); and M4.20 hands an unmet criterion to an M4.16 that does not own it (V4). ON THE COST LENS: nothing here changes any production request rate. The decorator is test-only over MemoryBinStore; it adds exactly one delegate request per call on the no-fault path, a second putIfAbsent only when duplicatePut fires, and put/getRange/multipart/delete pass straight through, as the row states. No request scales with records, shards, partitions or indices.

findings.line: 148-150 (the three putIfAbsent draws), 130-132 (fires), 218-220 (putIfMatch's two discarded alignment draws); the test that was supposed to pin it is FaultInjectingStoreTest.java:204-243, and the reason it does not is stated at FaultInjectingStore.java:111-113
findings.finding: SURVIVING MUTATIONS, MEASURED (3), all on the exact property R1 was raised about. R2 said three of the round's four fixes were pinned by no test; three tests were added, and the fourth fix -- the one R1 blocked on -- is still pinned by nothing. Against the whole sequencer suite (159 tests, 17 classes, including the unstaged simulation) each of these leaves it at 159 tests / 0 failures: (a) restore the lazy draw, i.e. move `boolean ambiguous`/`boolean duplicate` from 149-150 to after the unreachable throw at 154 -- that is the R1 defect reinstated verbatim, and the fix's own 11-line comment at 137-147 is left arguing for code that is no longer there; (b) make `fires` at 130-132 early-return false when `p == 0.0` -- that reinstates round 1's defect and falsifies both the javadoc at 72-83 ('drawn UNCONDITIONALLY ... so a disabled class consumes its own stream and no other class's fault positions move') and the one at 126-129 ('DRAWS EVEN WHEN p == 0'); (c) delete putIfMatch's two result-discarding draws at 218 and 220, whose comment at 211-217 says they exist for nothing but stream alignment. The new decorrelation test cannot see any of these because it measures `scramble` as a pure static function, and the comment at 111-113 says so explicitly: 'driving it through the store would measure the store's control flow as well as the streams'. But the store's control flow is precisely where R1's defect lived and where the fix went. What is unpinned is the toggle property itself, and it is cheap to pin without any statistics: run a fixed sequence of putIfAbsent calls twice at (0, 0.05, 0.05) and at (0.05, 0.05, 0.05), and assert the ambiguousPut and duplicatePut key lists are equal except for keys where unreachable fired -- I ran exactly that over 2000 seeds and it is true today (0 unexplained differences) and false under mutation (a).
findings.failure_scenario: Someone reads 148-150, sees three booleans computed and only the first used before a throw, and 'tidies' the two dead-until-later draws to the branches that consume them -- or reads putIfMatch:218-220, sees two calls whose return values are discarded, and deletes them as dead code. Either edit reinstates the aliasing R1 blocked on, the suite stays green, and M4.13's criterion 1 -- 'each injected fault class must have at least one seed where it CHANGES THE OUTCOME' -- becomes unobtainable again, because the sweep's toggle-one-class evidence can no longer be attributed to the class toggled. That is the third time this property has been shipped broken and caught only by a reviewer's measurement rather than by the suite.

findings.finding: The M4.12 row states 'WHAT THIS COMMIT CONTAINS, stated because an earlier draft of this row described a commit other than itself: the decorator and six unit tests of it.' FaultInjectingStoreTest.java has NINE @Test methods (grep -c '@Test' = 9; Gradle reports '9 tests completed'). The three the row does not count are the three added this round: theTHREEFaultStreamsAreINDEPENDENTCoinsAndNotOnePhaseLocked, aProbabilityOUTSIDEZeroToOneIsREFUSEDRatherThanSilentlyDisablingItsClass and aDUPLICATEDPutREALLYREACHESTheStoreTwiceAndTheFirstResultIsWhatTheCallerGets -- i.e. exactly the pins that close R2. So the sentence written to guarantee the row describes its own commit describes the PRE-FIX commit, and it is the same row and the same defect class R3 was raised about.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.15 is the milestone review and milestone-review reads backlog.md, which AGENTS.md calls authoritative. A reviewer at M4's completion condition reads 'the decorator and six unit tests of it', counts six, and concludes the round-3 majors about unpinned fixes were never closed -- or worse, trusts the count, does not open the file, and records that three fixes still need pinning when they do not. Either way the row is evidence and the evidence is wrong, which is the state this row's own opening warning exists to prevent.

findings.finding: The newly created M4.16 row ends '⚠️ ADR-0029 IS DRAFTED and weighs four options with their costs -- seal every unsealed ancestor (rejected: ...); fail a zombie's write on the LEASE ...; a RANGE SEAL ...; and minting the epoch only after start succeeds ...'. There is no ADR-0029 in the tree: docs/internal/product/decisions/ runs 0001-0028 and stops at 0028-three-shapes-in-the-commit-chain-behind-a-sealed-interface.md, and `grep -rn 'ADR-0029'` over the whole repository returns this backlog line and nothing else. The row asserts a drafted deliverable that does not exist, in the document AGENTS.md calls authoritative, in the same commit that adds the row. That is non-negotiable 4 ('never claim a test passes, a gate runs, or a number was measured, without having done it') applied to an artifact, and it is the unresolvable-ID defect AGENTS.md's Never list already names one step worse: the ID names nothing AND there is nothing to look up.
findings.failure_scenario: Whoever picks up M4.16 reads 'ADR-0029 IS DRAFTED', looks for it to review the four weighed options before implementing, finds nothing, and either redoes the analysis from scratch (the row's four bullets are a summary, not the ADR's cost numbers -- 'needs its number against the $52/month model' is explicitly unfinished) or, worse, treats the row's summary as the decision and implements the lease-fencing option without the ADR that non-negotiable 8 and the adr skill require for a change to the commit protocol. Meanwhile every status report on M4 reads 'the ADR is drafted', so nothing schedules writing it.

findings.finding: R4 is only half closed. M4.16 is now a row, but it is not a row that owns what M4.20 hands it. M4.20 says 'The faulted range needs its own floor, which is what M4.16's two deferred progress assertions become.' The M4.16 row at line 270 is entirely about the unsealed-abandoned-chain defect (LocalSequencer.start sealing only epoch-1) and contains no progress assertion, no faulted-range floor and no seed range. The two obligations R4 named -- the faulted-run progress assertions and the seed range -- are therefore still unowned; M4.13's row, which did absorb M4.12's other deferrals, does not mention them either. Note the M4.16 row itself is sound for every OTHER reference to it: CommitProtocolSimulationTest.java:103,108 and Invariants.java:288 / InvariantsTest.java:204 all refer to the unsealed-ancestor defect, which is exactly what the row describes.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.20 is implemented, its author reads 'M4.16's two deferred progress assertions', opens M4.16 and finds a row about chain sealing with no progress assertion in it. The best case costs a confused detour; the likely case is that the faulted-range floor is dropped as already-owned-elsewhere, and the sweep goes on reporting clean for seeds that committed zero -- the precise vacuity M4.20's own row measured (seed 17 commits zero and reports clean). Milder than R4 only because M4.20 is `todo` and states the gap in its own text, so it fails loudly rather than silently.

findings.finding: The M4.20 row's specification of what the driver must DO has been spliced into the middle of a defect note and is now grammatically attached to it: '⚠️ Also `withZone` returns `this`, violating the `Clock` contract -- many logical pods, one seed, through the `Sequencer` seam, with failover both ways (a polite release and a TTL lapse) and fenced leaders that do not know it yet.' Those are two unrelated statements -- a SimulatedClock contract violation, and the four things the simulation driver has to model -- joined by a dash that makes the second read as elaboration of the first. sdd.md makes the row the spec, and the four requirements in the second clause (many pods, one seed, through the seam, failover both ways) are the acceptance criteria for M4.20.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.20's author reads the row for its acceptance criteria, parses the sentence as one clause about withZone, and the four requirements after the dash are not read as requirements. The driver lands with, say, failover in one direction only, and nothing in the row is left to point at, because the sentence that asked for both directions was punctuated as commentary on a Clock method.

findings.finding: The M4.12 row's WHAT IS NOT MODELLED list is incomplete in a way that matters, because M4.13 is chartered to close exactly the gaps this list names. The row says 'putIfMatch (the lease's only CAS) gets `ambiguousPut` but never `unreachable`, so a lease CAS cannot fail cleanly' and 'put, getRange, multipart and delete inject nothing'. It does not say that `duplicatePut` also never fires on putIfMatch: line 220 draws the duplicate stream and discards the result, so a retried in-flight CAS -- a real object-store fault, and the one that would exercise a renew racing its own earlier attempt -- is unmodelled and unnamed. Related and also unstated: when ambiguousPut and duplicatePut both fire on the same putIfAbsent call, ambiguous wins and the duplicate is never recorded, so `injected()` under-reports duplicatePut by design and no comment says so.
findings.failure_scenario: M4.13 works down M4.12's stated gap list -- delayed writes, reordered completions, partitioned leaders, unreachable-on-putIfMatch -- closes every one, and reports the fault model complete. The duplicated conditional PUT against the lease is still missing, so the sweep can never produce the renew-races-its-own-retry interleaving, and the row that was supposed to be the record of what is not covered says nothing about it.
